description: Ex-RAF TE213, c/n CBAF.11274, built August 1945; delivered to the SAAF as 5518 and SOC April 1954, then gate guard at AFB Waterkloof for about 25 years. Rebuilt to fly 1987-1995 with Reutech sponsorship, first post-restoration flight 5 October 1995 wearing 5553/AX-K, later repainted 5518/AX-K. Crashed non-fatally at Swartkop on 15 April 2000 after engine failure and was crated. Restoration managed by the Friends of the SAAF Museum; FSAAFM confirmed in 2026 that a dedicated hangar is still being built for it, so the airframe is dismantled and not on public view. The very common listing of a Swartkop "Spitfire 5553" is this same aircraft under a marking it no longer wears.
museum_name: South African Air Force Museum Swartkop

description: THE SERIAL IT WEARS IS NOT ITS OWN. USAAF 44-72202, c/n 122-38661; to the Swedish Flygvapnet as J26 Fv 26112 from 1947, then to the Dominican Republic in 1952 as FAD 1917, sold 1984-85 to Brian O'Farrell / Johnson Aviation, Miami, and shipped to South Africa, arriving Cape Town docks 14 November 1987 and Lanseria dismantled 19 November 1987. Restored over about twelve years, flew again 1998, damaged in a wheels-up landing at Swartkop in 2001 after undercarriage failure. It is painted as SAAF 325, a Korean-War 2 Squadron Mustang serial it never carried; the airframe never served with the SAAF. year_built left blank: Aerial Visuals says "circa 1944" construction while the museum's own page says delivered September 1945 - not settled.
